title: Priority wavefront admission and attention tiling
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Objective: Reduce 99th and 99.9th percentile end-to-end latency for mixed prefill+decode workloads by combining a priority 'wavefront' admission policy with an attention-tiling prefetch strategy and opportunistic kernel probing. Motivation: Current continuous batching handles average throughput well but exhibits long tails for heterogeneous request shapes and bursts that intermix long prefill requests with short chat turns. We need a low-risk runtime change that (1) improves tail latency without sacrificing throughput, (2) plays nicely with kernel selection heuristics, and (3) is rollable via canary. Key idea: when admitting prefill requests into a batch, tag each request with a wavefront priority derived from deadline, model shape, and observed per-tenant tail-profile. Admission then proceeds in a multi-pass wavefront: (a) fast-path wave for short/interactive requests (high priority), (b) standard coalesce wave for throughput, and (c) deferred wave for long prefill-heavy requests that can be split or serviced on a slower kernel path. Attention tiling: introduce a lightweight prefetcher that computes attention tile hints during prefill and stores compact attention-shard metadata in the KV cache header. During decode, kernel selection consults tile hints to choose tiled attention kernels when beneficial (lower memory pressure, better warp utilization). Kernel probing: add an opportunistic kernel probe step at admission to sample latency predictions across a short window (20-50ms) and attach a preferred-kernel hint to the request. We expect this to reduce kernel mis-selection for heterogenous shapes. Tradeoffs: extra admission CPU cycles and bookkeeping vs tail reduction; potential increased memory churn from tile metadata. Implementation plan: 1) spec data structures and proto for wavefront priority and tile hint (low-level binary header, backward-compatible). 2) implement admission wavefront scheduler with configurable thresholds and fallbacks. 3) attention-tiling prefetch worker that runs during prefill and annotates KV entries. 4) kernel probe runner that uses lightweight microbenchmarks on sampled batches. 5) integration: admission consults kernel hints + tiling hints and annotates request for the decode scheduler. 6) experiments and calibration with synthetic mix and production sampling. Success metrics (target): - p99 end-to-end latency reduction of 20% for mixed workloads - p99.9 reduction of 25% - <5% throughput regression for 95% of profiles - CPU admission overhead <6% of request CPU budget - No regression on single-tenant large-batch throughput Rollout: feature gating via config flag and runtime-1.25 canary pipeline. Backout path: revert flag; admission defaults to current coalescer. Monitoring: dashboard for per-tenant p50/p95/p99/p99.9, kernel-mismatch-rate, tile-hit-rate, admission-cpu-ops, and memorialized logs for deferred wave items.
acceptance_criteria: Deployed canary that shows >=15% p99 reduction on test-mix in canary region
Config flag to enable/disable wavefront admission at runtime
Attention tile metadata added without causing KV header size regressions >=10%
Kernel-mismatch-rate reduced by >=30% on sampled heterogeneous shapes
Automated e2e regression test covering strict SLA tenant (latency budget) passes
Documentation of data proto and operator-facing knobs in infra guide
test_plan: Unit tests for wavefront priority assignment, integration tests for multi-pass admission, microbenchmarks for kernel probe accuracy, load tests with synthetic mixes (short-chat heavy, prefill-heavy, mixed). Run A/B canary with 5% traffic for 48h, collect p50/p95/p99/p99.9, kernel-mismatch-rate, and tile-hit-rate. Validate admission CPU overhead using per-request tracing. Run stability test for 7 days on staging with scaled production traffic replay.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind runtime feature flag. 2) Deploy to canary cluster (runtime-1.25-canary) with 5% traffic for 48h. 3) If canary stable and meets targets, increase to 25% for 24h, then 100% in non-critical regions. 4) Gradual enable for SLA-critical tenants with opt-in for first week. 5) Monitor dashboards and set automated rollback if p99 increases >5% or CPU budget increase >10%.
